races.name: Kilbeggan Irish Whiskey Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose best form arrived on flat fast ground (won a 1m on Good at Southwell), now stepping into jumping; 96-day absence, tongue-strap fitted, and his hurdles form shows five finishes out of the money — needs a strong gallop to fire which this race may not supply.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, six-year-old with 26 days between runs and a trainer hitting form at 1/6 over the fortnight; his 11-run record on similar going shows one win and four places, but the uncontested lead here is a significant asset.

runners_data.name: All Night Revival
runners_data.note: PJ Rothwell-trained six-year-old whose history shows a string of fourth-place finishes on Good ground; running style is unclassified (U), has not won in five starts at this trip, and the 72-day absence is a mild flag on fitness.

runners_data.name: Chantilly Wings
runners_data.note: Good form figures across five runs at up to 20f on Good ground and one placing, but 308 days off the track is the standout concern; a natural front-runner who will struggle to get his customary berth with Hillhead Runner dominant, limiting his chance in the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Front-running type who placed on Good recently but has been pushed back on the map because the prominent berths are oversubscribed; the 56-day break is manageable and his 2/16f/Good run is his best, but Ben Harvey riding a horse racing away from its optimal position makes this tricky.

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Paddy Cody (7lb claim) aboard for Eoin Doyle, who has been quiet at 0/4 over 14 days; the horse's 2/19f/Good last time out is his most relevant piece of form, travels prominently and handles this trip and ground combination — the most straightforward profile in the field to read.

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard firing at 6/44 over a fortnight, and Penny Express has placed three times from nine runs on similar going; versatile enough to race prominently or off the pace, the "h" headgear note and hg:h style hint at a horse that can settle, useful in a race where a tactical gallop may not stretch the field.

runners_data.name: Urinmydreams
runners_data.note: J J Slevin in the saddle but this is a horse who has finished between 8th and 15th in all five recent starts on Good ground; the ⚠ fade flag is significant, hold-up style, lowest OR in the field at 77, and needs a pace collapse that this race is unlikely to provide.

races.paceDynamic: Hillhead Runner is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious rival willing to press him from the front, he should be allowed to dictate at a fair but unforced gallop on Good to Firm ground over 2m2½f at Kilbeggan. Imarajan and Penny Express are the genuine prominent types capable of tracking him in second and third, creating a structured, evenly-run race rather than a searching test of stamina. Georg Zhukov and Urinmydreams operate from hold-up positions but the latter's consistent fade in the finish makes him an unlikely beneficiary, leaving Zhukov as the sole credible late mover. Chantilly Wings and Codger's Rock are both natural prominent racers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field carries more pace than the front can accommodate — Hillhead Runner and Imarajan are best placed to actually secure their positions, with Chantilly Wings and Codger's Rock likely to race slightly further back than ideal. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting a controlled pace on fast ground — strongly favours prominent horses who travel smoothly and have the class to kick when the leader is challenged from the second-last, rather than late-closers who need a strong gallop to get into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hillhead Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Hillhead Runner leads unchallenged and sets a sustainable gallop that stretches the field without emptying the tank.
scenarios.body: Hillhead Runner dictates every yard, the race stays together until the second-last, and only the horses travelling closest to him have the petrol to challenge; prominent trackers who transit smoothly from chase to kick benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hillhead Runner's lead is pressured or he fades from the second-last, allowing a stalking horse to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Imarajan or Penny Express, travelling smoothly just off the pace, attacks between the last two hurdles and the weakening leader cannot resist; both have placed form on similar Good ground and the trip suits their profiles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the front end goes faster than expected and sets up a slowly-run, then-quickened race that drains the leaders inside the final flight.
scenarios.body: Georg Zhukov, the sole credible hold-up horse with any form, closes into a weakening field; the Good to Firm surface aids his finishing effort if the pace has been genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the lead aggressively early, turning the race into an attrition contest that suits neither front-runners nor closers.
scenarios.body: Codger's Rock or Chantilly Wings, despite being mapped away from their natural positions, forces an unplanned pace battle that unwinds the field; a resolute stayer who handles the chaos profits at long odds.

watchPoints.text: Chantilly Wings has been off the track for 308 days — watch for any signs of rustiness at the start or through the early stages, as a sluggish jump could cost it vital ground from its natural prominent position.

Hillhead Runner's STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) flags that it may race out of role today — if it fails to stride on early and another runner edges it for the lead, the entire pace map collapses and the race becomes unpredictable.

Codger's Rock and Chantilly Wings are both natural prominent runners squeezed into midfield on the map — if either pushes forward aggressively to reclaim their natural berth, the early pace could quicken unexpectedly and compromise Hillhead Runner's rhythm.

Georg Zhukov's hold-up style and absence of 96 days make him the key watch for whether closers can get competitive — if he fails to travel with any fluency in the final mile, Scenario C is effectively off the table.

Urinmydreams has faded in every recent start and is ridden by the highest-profile jockey in the field (J J Slevin) — monitor whether Slevin attempts to change tactics and ride more prominently, which would add unexpected pace pressure to the front end.

races.name: Writech Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with licence to dictate from the front; OR 135 is the joint-highest in the race, and his two wins at similar trip on good ground are significant, but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence as he is marginally stepping up in company from his comfort zone.|

runners_data.name: Gameball
runners_data.note: Six-year-old trained by De Bromhead with strong good-ground credentials — three of his four runs on similar going produced a place or better, and he drops back from a 71-day break looking fresh; natural prominent runner ideally suited to sitting a length or two off a lone front-runner.|

runners_data.name: Bottler'secret
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from a 195-day absence for a small yard (T14: 1/15) with a concerning record on good or firmer ground, all five similar-going runs producing finishes of 4th or worse; needs a searching pace that this shape is unlikely to provide.|

runners_data.name: Kamikaz Du Plessis
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained six-year-old wearing a tongue-strap, with an outstanding record on good ground (9 of 10 runs producing a place or win); the fall on his most recent run is worth noting but his overall profile is compelling for a prominent racer at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Stede Bonnet
runners_data.note: Another Elliott runner who has won twice and placed three times from his last five completed starts, though all that form came on softer ground; legitimate prominent type with a fitness edge (32 days since last run) but the step up to good-to-firm conditions is an unresolved question.|

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Won twice and placed three times at this trip on good ground historically, but his last two runs at Kilbeggan produced finishes of 9th and 10th, suggesting course form is not straightforwardly positive; trainer yard is quiet (T14: 0/2) and he is carrying 158lbs.|

runners_data.name: Harry Des Ongrais
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old who has been absent 138 days and has never placed on anything faster than heavy ground across five similar-going runs; amateur claim (7lb claimer) does not compensate for the stiff going concern, and the yard has had zero runners in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Won his most recent start over course and distance on good ground and has four other placed efforts at similar trips; races from the back and needs a contested pace to reel in leaders, which is possible but not guaranteed given the race shape — the 5lb claimer is a slight concern.|

runners_data.name: Gin Tonic
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced five-year-old with course-and-distance form (won 2m on good ground) and placed on the same trip; Paul Nolan's yard has been quiet (T14: 0/3) but this is a horse whose form figures at this trip on fast ground are the best in the race proportionally.|

runners_data.name: Lisnamult Lad
runners_data.note: Front-running nine-year-old who has been running in spots off just six days' rest, but his natural style makes the mapped midfield position misleading — genuinely wants to be prominent but cannot get there in this crowded, pace-heavy field; recent form figures of P9P-P0 are discouraging.|

runners_data.name: Littlefoot
runners_data.note: Won twice from five runs at around 2m on good or soft ground and wears a hood; prominent type who finished 1st just 56 days ago and is likely to track the leader naturally without having to fight for position, making him a realistic each-way contender in Scenario A.|

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form most recently over 2m on good ground and Harry Cobden taking the ride is an immediate upgrade signal; a natural front-runner who will push forward despite the redistribution mapping, and his excellent good-ground record (3 wins, 6 places from 10 similar-going runs) makes him dangerous if he secures a forward berth.|

runners_data.name: Nelson Muntz
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed on good ground twice at shorter trips; all five recent runs at 2m produced mid-pack finishes and he has never won beyond 2m, so the step up to 2m4f is an untested stamina question rather than a definite positive.|

runners_data.name: Faceman
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m4f on good ground and has 3 wins and 6 places from 14 similar-going runs — the most consistently good-ground form in the field; his natural prominent style means he will push forward from his mapped midfield position, and the yard (T14: 1/7) has had a recent winner.|

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing a tongue-strap, raced just seven days ago, and has placed three times on good ground from nine runs; carries 145lbs and the short turnaround combined with a style that needs a true gallop makes it hard to see him winning unless the pace scenario changes dramatically.|

runners_data.name: Ryan's Son
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground as a five-year-old and has decent recent form figures on fast surfaces, but his last two completed starts produced a 12th and a 6th; the redistribution to midfield reflects a field too full of forward-going types for him to secure his preferred position.|

runners_data.name: Moon Mission
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground and placed at 2m1f on similar; his most recent win came on the same trip and going profile and the trainer (T14: 1/26) has recent activity; however, he is mapped out of position and will need to manoeuvre through a congested early pack to get to the front.|

runners_data.name: Has Me Dreaming
runners_data.note: Returning from a remarkable 674-day absence — that alone makes him extremely difficult to assess; showed promise with a win and a third from his two career runs on good ground, both at shorter trips, but the layoff is a massive unknown and the jockey booking has not been confirmed.|

races.paceDynamic: Thecompanysergeant is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 18 and, with no genuine rival pushing for the early lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Kilbeggan. That measured tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, meaning the race will be run at a pace that suits those racing prominently just off the leader rather than deep hold-up horses who need a genuine test to close late. Gameball, Kamikaz Du Plessis, Stede Bonnet, Littlefoot and Gin Tonic are all legitimate prominent types who can track the leader comfortably, giving them a decisive tactical edge in this shape. The field contains a significant surplus of horses whose natural style is prominent or front-running — Lisnamult Lad, Paul's Dream, Faceman, Ryan's Son, Moon Mission and Has Me Dreaming have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all occupy their preferred position — with Faceman and Paul's Dream, both in career-best form, most likely to press closer than their mapped position suggests. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominently behind a single, uncontested leader and produce a clean, well-timed run from the second-last hurdle, rather than closers who will find the pace insufficient to reel in those racing on the bridle throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Thecompanysergeant sets a steady pace and two or three prominent trackers sit within two lengths throughout before kicking on from two out.
scenarios.body: Gameball and Kamikaz Du Plessis are ideally placed to stalk the leader at a controlled tempo on ground that suits both, arriving unanticipated by deeper rivals who never get into the race; the modest gallop means class and position count for everything at Kilbeggan's sharp finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Thecompanysergeant is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged and the gallop is genuinely slow, draining finishing kick from those behind.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to press him, Thecompanysergeant could effectively turn this into a solo exercise at a pace entirely of his own choosing, his jumping accuracy and good-ground form making him hard to reel in late; prominent trackers are best placed to chase him home if he is caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently from three out to string the field out and create genuine gaps for hold-up horses to exploit in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ad Caelum has strong good-ground form at this trip and has been building back to form, and Nelson Muntz and Rexem could both find more than their recent efforts suggest if they get a clear run at the last; however, the modest likely tempo makes this a genuinely difficult scenario for true closers to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the numerous natural front-runners redistributed to midfield push up aggressively early, creating a contested pace that disrupts the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Faceman and Paul's Dream, both in excellent form and temperamentally keen to race prominently, could surge forward and transform the pace into something more searching, gifting an opportunity to a resolute stayer like Ad Caelum or Gin Tonic who relishes a genuine test; this is structurally possible but requires multiple horses to override their mapped positions simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Thecompanysergeant is the sole confirmed pacemaker — if he is allowed to bowled along completely unchallenged, watch whether prominent trackers Gameball and Kamikaz Du Plessis take him on from the third-last or sit and wait, as that decision will define the entire race outcome.

Faceman and Paul's Dream are natural front-runners shown in midfield on the pace map — watch whether either pushes forward aggressively at the start to reclaim their preferred position, as that would immediately alter the pace dynamic and benefit horses with stamina.

Has Me Dreaming returns from 674 days off the track with no confirmed jockey; any significant market move in the ring should be treated as meaningful insider information about fitness, as the formbook is essentially useless for this runner.

Ad Caelum is the only true hold-up horse with a recent course-and-distance win on good ground — if the pace is genuinely modest he may arrive too late, but watch whether Michael Kenneally (5lb claimer) positions him closer than expected to compensate.

Stede Bonnet and Grann's Boy both carry prominent-style profiles but have unresolved going questions — all their competitive form came on soft or heavy — and if either appears to be travelling poorly from the fifth-last hurdle on the good-to-firm surface, discount them immediately.

races.name: Kilmurray Group Midlands National Handicap Chase (Listed)

runners_data.name: Amirite
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner at OR 142 for De Bromhead; handles good ground (1W2P in similar conditions) and has won over 26f, but the 34f trip and 90-day absence are queries — the pace role is his but the style-fit flag tempers confidence in a finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Perceval Legallois
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's consistent performer has six placed runs in good-ground similar conditions but has been well beaten recently; 46 days fresh and 165lbs are manageable, though the soft-heavy form profile is more flattering than the good-ground record.

runners_data.name: Uncle Pat
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins on a horse with three wins from five similar-going starts and back-to-back placed runs over staying trips; the 1/32f/GOO most recent run is the standout piece of form in this race and the trip is no concern.

runners_data.name: Native Speaker
runners_data.note: Three wins and six places from ten good-ground runs makes this De Bromhead runner extremely well-suited to conditions; a strong pace-tracking profile and a recent win (1/24f/GOO) make him one of the most credible prominent operators in the field.

runners_data.name: Boston Rover
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's unexposed chaser has won three times on good ground and was unbeaten in a hot streak before a pulled-up run; the 264-day layoff is a significant concern and Sam Ewing's handling of a returning horse in a 17-runner listed handicap will be tested.

runners_data.name: Olympic Man
runners_data.note: Consistently fails to fire on good ground (0W1P from seven similar-going starts) and the P6P5F form string does nothing to raise confidence; the amateur rider and modest trainer 14-day strike rate add further dampeners.

runners_data.name: Solitary Man
runners_data.note: E Bolger's veteran has three wins and six places from ten good-ground outings and finished 4th and 1st in his last two good-ground starts; a natural prominent type who should find a position just behind the pace, and this track and trip combination suits.

runners_data.name: Raglan Road
runners_data.note: Cobden takes a notable booking for De Bromhead and this horse's two most recent wins have come on good ground, but it is a prominent-style runner that the race map has squeezed into midfield — getting into its preferred position in a field this congested is the central challenge.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Recent form (95U-75) is uninspiring, and while he is a natural front-runner at heart, he has been pushed into midfield on this map simply because there is no room for him near the pace; shorter trips and easier ground suit him better.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Place
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on good ground last time out for Bolger but has been inconsistent; wears a hood and at OR 130 carries 154lbs — a genuine prominent type that cannot get near the pace in this shape, making the hat of headgear and weight a compounding problem.

runners_data.name: Yoradreamer
runners_data.note: Mullins's lightly-weighted 7yo has placed twice on good ground and was 2nd most recently over 25f/GOO, but his natural front-rank inclinations are frustrated here — a field with this many prominent types leaves him racing at a disadvantage to his style.

runners_data.name: Shanbally Kid
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in the Mullins yard with a warning flag for fading in the finish; has pulled up in three of last five starts and the good-ground record (1W1P) is modest — genuine closing effort would require a much more strung-out race than this map projects.

runners_data.name: Will Do
runners_data.note: Dismal recent form (0P0PP) across good, soft and heavy ground; a prominent type in profile but displaced here, and Gordon Elliott's 69-day freshen-up has not yielded results consistently with this runner — hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: Invictus Machin
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh's booking for Cromwell is interesting on a horse that has placed twice on good ground and won once in similar conditions; wears a hood, and though squeezed into midfield by redistribution, Walsh's experience at getting horses competitive may partially offset the positional disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Lonesome Boatman
runners_data.note: Won over 28f/GOO and placed three times in similar conditions, giving him one of the more relevant form profiles in the race; 129 days off is the query, and the absence of a named jockey in the data is a concern for a horse that needs positive placement.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Has run 13 times on good ground with two places and no wins, which is a modest return; wears a visor and at OR 126 is at the bottom of the weights, but the form string (8647-0) going the wrong way and no jockey listed makes this a speculative interest at best.

runners_data.name: A Penny A Hundred
runners_data.note: Mullins's lightly-framed 7yo has a placed record on good ground (1W4P) but recent form has dipped; the hold-up style suits a scenario where the race develops into a true stamina test, though the 3m1½f at OR 125 and 149lbs is a step into new territory.

races.paceDynamic: Amirite is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at OR 142 with De Bromhead's confidence behind him, will stride into the lead from the outset and set a measured, controlled gallop over this 3m1½f trip on Good to Firm ground — crucially, he will not be pressured into setting a true test because no other runner has a genuine lead mandate. The field is saturated with prominent-style horses — Raglan Road, Drumgill, Pride Of Place, Yoradreamer, Will Do, Invictus Machin, and Lonesome Boatman are all natural front-rank types who cannot all get their position, meaning several will be shuffled back to a midfield they did not choose and will race out of role throughout. Behind Amirite, Uncle Pat (Townend/Mullins), Native Speaker and Solitary Man are the established prominent operators most likely to actually secure the positions nearest the pace, with the redistributed cluster forced to track or settle deeper than ideal. This race shape — a sustainable lead, minimal pressure, and a field of prominent types forced wide or back — strongly favours horses who can travel fluently in the first four and produce a clean jump at the last, making the racing-prominently-on-good-ground profile the dominant winning template.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amirite Controls, Stays Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Amirite bowls along uncontested and the prominent horses immediately behind him — Uncle Pat and Native Speaker — track him at a comfortable clip into the straight.
scenarios.body: Amirite dictates every yard on going he handles and jumps clean throughout, ensuring the race is run at a tempo that never exposes stamina limits; Uncle Pat and Native Speaker, travelling into contention from true prominent positions, are best placed to pounce late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poachers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is even more modest than expected and a cluster of true prominent types manage to get into rhythm just off Amirite heading into the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Solitary Man, who has won and placed repeatedly on good ground from a prominent position, and Raglan Road — the redistributed prominent type most likely of that group to actually muscle into the front rank — both thrive when the race becomes a jumping test rather than a stamina grind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Staying Test
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively quick enough to string the field and the hold-up runners get into the race off a genuine gallop in the final mile.
scenarios.body: Shanbally Kid and A Penny A Hundred, operating from genuine hold-up positions in a Mullins yard that knows how to place them, could benefit if attrition at the fences catches the front rank — though Shanbally Kid's tendency to fade late is a concern even in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent positions create early interference, jumping errors or fallers that reshuffle the race entirely from the second circuit.
scenarios.body: In a 17-runner handicap chase on a sharp track with multiple horses fighting for the same ground, a surviving hold-up or mid-pack type could inherit a winning position by default; Moonovercloon and Lonesome Boatman, both racing off realistic marks, are the names to watch if the field thins dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Amirite's jumping under Paul Townend — if he makes a significant error at any of the early fences, the entire race dynamic collapses and the midfield-shuffled prominent types will have no pace to track.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types (Raglan Road, Drumgill, Pride Of Place, Yoradreamer, Will Do, Invictus Machin) all attempting to find positions in the first circuit of a 17-runner field on a sharp track — watch for crowding, clipping of heels and early casualties at the fences.

Boston Rover returns from 264 days off in a listed handicap; horses returning from long absences who were formerly progressive can run well fresh, but any sign of ring-rustiness in the jumping phase will end his chance immediately.

Uncle Pat under Paul Townend — Mullins's No.1 jockey on the stable's most credible runner; if Townend positions him second or third from early on, that is the clearest signal this horse is being targeted for the race.

Solitary Man's jumping accuracy at the first few fences — he has the form and conditions to go close, but his ability to slot cleanly into a prominent position from stall in a crowded early-pace scenario will determine whether his good-ground profile can be activated.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Centreofattention
runners_data.note: Poorly-in-form hurdler making her chasing debut (form /670-8), Bolger sending her into a 3m1½f beginners chase; a genuine hold-up operator whose actual closing run will be compromised by being pushed into midfield in this relatively small field, and three wins in six similar-going starts counts for little given the step into chasing.|

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Meade runner with a blinker-free profile who has shown occasional placing form on Good ground (13 runs, 1W4P in similar conditions), but his instinct to race from the rear means the midfield slot he is mapped into does not reflect how he wants to be ridden; a beginners chase trip of 3m1½f suits on paper, though recent form (PP0P-4) offers little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Franciscan Rock
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR 136, Morris sends just the one runner here which often signals purpose; nine runs on Good or similar ground returning 1W4P is solid, though a 71-day absence and tongue-tie suggest he needs to rediscover form shown when second over 21f last time out. A fluent jumper could use class late.|

runners_data.name: Juke Hill
runners_data.note: Elliott runner on just 10 days' turnaround — the freshness angle matters here — carrying a hood (b) which has been tried previously; form of 557-84 is modest but the quick reappearance suggests the team feel he is cherry-ripe. Going form is thin (0W1P in 6 similar-ground runs) and he needs to find more at these OR levels.|

runners_data.name: Kevin's Pride
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: one confirmed front-runner, tongue-tie and cheekpieces (tp) retained, winning on Good ground over 20f last time and placed twice at 20-24f on similar; McConnell has a modest 14-day strike rate but Slevin booking is a significant upgrade. His entire chance rests on dictating an uncontested pace — the race is built around him.|

runners_data.name: Orkneys Jack
runners_data.note: Amateur rider (Mr JP Sampson, 7lb claim) in a competitive beginners chase is a concern, and the flag fades-in-finish warning is important over 3m1½f; going form is limited (0W1P in 4 Good-ground runs) and Young's stable has 0/1 in the 14-day window. A horse that struggles to sustain his effort late is poorly suited to this trip.|

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Second Elliott runner alongside Juke Hill, also returning quickly (10 days), wearing a tongue-tie (t); form of 3-2234 is the most consistent in the field and 9/13 in similar going conditions (1W5P) shows real adaptability. Will press forward from a prominent position and represents the most likely challenger to Kevin's Pride if the leader weakens.|

runners_data.name: Tonaghneave Well
runners_data.note: Cromwell stable in fine 14-day form (7/55) and Keith Donoghue takes the ride, both positive angles; however form of 669-89 over the last five runs is deeply uninspiring and his best placing on similar ground came at a sprint trip by comparison. Prominent style suits the race shape in theory, but the class and form questions are significant at this OR 116 level.|

races.paceDynamic: Kevin's Pride is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead from the outset, JJ Slevin can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits over this 3m1½f trip on Good to Firm ground. Scalpnagoon and Tonaghneave Well will push forward from prominent positions and ensure Kevin's Pride is not entirely unchallenged, but neither has the profile to seriously dispute control, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than frenetic. The hold-up brigade of Franciscan Rock, Juke Hill, Centreofattention, and Charlie Luciano will settle in behind, though Centreofattention and Charlie Luciano — true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map — are unlikely to secure their natural rear-of-field position in a field this compact, meaning their closing kicks may arrive earlier than ideal. This race shape strongly favours the prominent, front-running profile: a leader with a clear, uncontested line over an extended trip on quick ground, where stamina and jumping fluency at the head of affairs will be harder to reel in than a late swooper can manage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kevin's Pride Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kevin's Pride jumps cleanly and Slevin controls tempo from the front, trading on his stamina.
scenarios.body: Kevin's Pride dictates throughout, sets an honest but measured gallop, and the effort to peg him back from off the pace proves too great on Good to Firm ground over this marathon trip; a clean round of jumping seals it. Front-running and prominent types who can handle the pace being set from the front are the prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Kevin's Pride makes a jumping error or weakens after the last, allowing a prominent tracker to swoop.
scenarios.body: Scalpnagoon has shown consistent form over shorter but builds here as a close tracker, and Tonaghneave Well, despite a poor recent string, could creep into contention if conditions and trip unlock latent ability. Either would need Kevin's Pride to falter at a fence or tie up on the run-in to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stayer Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and front horses flatten out, leaving a grinding stayer to come through.
scenarios.body: Franciscan Rock, carrying the highest OR in the field at 136, has course-type form and the class to pick up pieces if those ahead have burned too much fuel; the Morris yard sends only one runner here, suggesting intent. Juke Hill has the fitness edge with just 10 days since his last run and could also stay on as others tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the redistributed hold-up types manage to produce a late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Centreofattention or Charlie Luciano — both true hold-up horses mapped forward out of role — finding a late gear, which is structurally unlikely given their style mismatch and recent poor form; Centreofattention has not placed in five chase runs and Charlie Luciano is 0-from-recent in similar company. The probability is low precisely because the horses best suited to it are not racing in their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Kevin's Pride is the fulcrum of the entire race — watch his jumping from the second fence onward; a bad error or awkward round will instantly hand Scalpnagoon and Franciscan Rock a route back into contention.

Orkneys Jack is flagged as fading in the finish and carries an amateur rider over 3m1½f on quick ground — monitor him from the third-last as a potential faller or loose horse risk that could interfere with runners tracking him.

Scalpnagoon and Juke Hill both return on just 10 days' rest for Gordon Elliott — watch how they travel in the middle stages; if either looks laboured before three out, Elliott's double entry may be running one as a pacemaker for the other.

Franciscan Rock's jumping at pace will be the tell — he has the class to win this but a 71-day absence means he may need to see out the early fences before his stamina engine kicks in; watch his fluency at the open ditch for a read on his sharpness.

races.name: Larrigy's Pub Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with A J Martin's yard in modest 14-day form (1/9); best sim-going run was 10th from 14, suggesting moderate aptitude for conditions, and a 33-day break is not a concern but getting a clear run from deep in a 19-runner field is the central tactical problem.

runners_data.name: Backwithyourown
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, which is its primary asset; John Burke's yard has gone 0/2 in the last 14 days and the horse holds a style-fit flag for racing out of role — the role here is front-running, which is its natural position, so discount the flag; the key question is whether it can sustain the lead over 2m2½f on quick ground.

runners_data.name: Kentucky Bluebird
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up type has gone 0W0P across seven sim-going runs, a notably blank record on good ground; 44 days since last run is acceptable but with no prominent finish in this going band it is hard to build a case.

runners_data.name: Scathach
runners_data.note: Unclassified style from Ross O'Sullivan's in-form yard (4/20 last 14 days); best run in similar going was a third from five starts but the hurdle form string includes a fall, and the awkward style tag makes tactical positioning uncertain in a big field.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on good ground in this hist (one win from 15 sim-going runs) and carries a hood; Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride which is a significant positive, and racing from off the pace gives him options in a race where the midfield may become congested.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Returned just six days ago and Jack Gilligan (5lb claim) partners this prominent runner who won over 18f on good; 13 sim-going runs with one win and four places is a respectable strike rate, and natural pace means it should get a clean position close to Backwithyourown without being squeezed out.

runners_data.name: Notmiwadi
runners_data.note: 284 days off the track is the headline concern before any shape discussion; a genuine back-of-the-field horse pushed into the midfield map by the volume of hold-up runners — the long absence and 0W0P on sim going over four runs suggest this is a difficult pitch at a competitive rating.

runners_data.name: Vairue
runners_data.note: 589 days absent — by far the longest layoff in the field — and the form string shows a single win buried in a 15-run sim-going sample; the horse tends to fade in finishes and returning from near-two-year absence in a 19-runner handicap off OR 86 is a formidable ask.

runners_data.name: Monty's Way
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old wearing a hood-and-tongue-strap combination; a natural hold-up runner pushed forward on the map by field congestion, the horse has gone 0/0 for George Stanley in the last 14 days and has three consecutive non-completions or tailed-off efforts in recent form — very little to work with.

runners_data.name: Boston Bobby
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on good ground (1W2P from 14 sim-going runs) and comes back after 31 days; a genuine hold-up horse wearing a hood, mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, and P J Rothwell's yard has been active (3/28 last 14 days) which offers mild encouragement, though the style displacement hurts its scenario fit.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old back after just six days, which warrants monitoring; Ben Harvey partners this prominent type from Adrian McGuinness's yard (2/28 last 14), and the recent form shows two third-place finishes at longer trips suggesting this 2m2½f trip should be well within range.

runners_data.name: Maybe Someday
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has gone 0W0P across five sim-going starts with two headgear pieces; a hold-up horse mapped forward by field overcrowding, and the combination of amateur rider (7lb claim) and an uninspiring form string makes this one of the harder cases to argue.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Form string reads 00-0PP, with two recent non-completions and 0W0P from seven sim-going starts; a genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield by the surplus of rear-division runners, Anna McGuinness claiming 7lbs is positive but the raw evidence is unpromising.

runners_data.name: Gold Gatewood
runners_data.note: 409 days off the track, only three sim-going starts on record, and J J Slevin provides the one significant upside; the hold-up style and the extreme layoff make this a speculative proposition, though Slevin's ability to produce horses cold is always worth noting.

runners_data.name: Wings Of Africa
runners_data.note: 0W0P from three sim-going starts and a form string containing two non-completions; a hold-up horse displaced forward on the map, trained by W J Lanigan whose yard has had one runner in the past 14 days — hard to find a structural angle.

runners_data.name: Chesterbaylad
runners_data.note: Second in a sim-going run (2/16f/GOO) is the best evidence in the book; a hold-up horse in a field oversupplied with them, Josh Younge's 7lb claim offers weight relief but 0W1P from 15 sim-going starts is a thin platform for optimism.

runners_data.name: High Notions
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 99 with a 1W2P sim-going record; no jockey listed which is a practical flag, but the rating, trip and going profile are all legitimate — the structural issue is that a hold-up style in a race with only one front-runner asks for a contested pace that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who ran just seven days ago, which raises fitness questions in the opposite direction to the long absentees; Anthony Mullins trains and the sim-going record shows 0W2P from 15 starts — consistent without winning, and at OR 88 faces a stiff challenge.

runners_data.name: Annarubyrose
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a genuine shape fit — second from seven sim-going starts and twice placed at 22f on good ground; Ian Patrick Donoghue's yard has placed 2/17 in the last 14 days, wears a hood, and the horse is well suited to tracking Backwithyourown closely and challenging from the second-last.

races.paceDynamic: Backwithyourown is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no serious early pressure to contest the lead — Georginas Jet and Annarubyrose will push to race prominently but neither is a natural pace-setter, meaning Backwithyourown can control tempo from the front on its own terms. On good-to-firm ground over 2m2½f at Kilbeggan, a single uncontested leader typically sets a honest but manageable gallop, which historically compresses the field through the early stages and rewards those tracking in the first five to eight. The field is heavily populated with hold-up horses — Notmiwadi, Monty's Way, Boston Bobby, Maybe Someday, Not So Serious, Gold Gatewood and Wings Of Africa are all genuine come-from-behind types who have been redistributed into the midfield map because there is simply not enough natural pace ahead of them to accommodate their preferred position; in practice, most will be further back than their mapped slot suggests. This race shape strongly favours prominent or close-tracking runners who can sit just behind the lone front-runner, travel with minimal cover issues, and produce their effort from the second-last hurdle — hold-up horses face a significant structural disadvantage unless the early tempo is truly punishing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Backwithyourown Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Backwithyourown dictates a sustainable gallop from the front and no rival applies significant pressure through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: Eoin Walsh settles Backwithyourown into a rhythm on the bridle, setting a fair but unhurried pace that leaves the hold-up brigade with little to aim at off the home turn; those tracking prominently in the first three will have enough energy reserves to challenge and sustain their run from the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Movers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Georginas Jet, Granlahan or Annarubyrose push forward aggressively and the race is run at a genuinely strong pace from an early stage.
scenarios.body: A hot early gallop stretches the field, exposing the large hold-up cohort who find themselves with too much ground to make up on good-to-firm ground where there is limited late juice; the prominent duo of Georginas Jet and Annarubyrose, both proven at this trip on good ground, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Punches Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely end-to-end and the field fans wide on the home turn, creating enough daylight for a deep closer to thread through.
scenarios.body: High Notions is the highest-rated runner in the field and carries a strong sim-going record; Goin' also has course-relevant form and would benefit from a messy contested gallop that leaves the prominent horses emptying late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the field dawdles in the early and middle stages behind Backwithyourown, leaving the leader fully fresh at the top of the home straight with an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: With no serious challenger and good-to-firm ground rewarding economical jumping, Backwithyourown simply finds nothing coming to challenge within range off the home turn and has enough in reserve to hold every challenger; Georginas Jet, closest to the pace throughout, is best placed of those giving chase.

watchPoints.text: Backwithyourown holds no natural challenger for the early lead — if Eoin Walsh elects to go fast, the race could be over as a contest before the home turn, catching the hold-up heavy field flat-footed.

At least seven horses listed as hold-up types have been redistributed into midfield on the pace map — in a 19-runner field on a tight track like Kilbeggan, congestion and traffic issues between the second-last and last hurdle are a genuine risk for deep closers including Notmiwadi, Boston Bobby and Gold Gatewood.

Three runners — Vairue (589 days), Gold Gatewood (409 days) and Notmiwadi (284 days) — return from very extended absences; any one of them moving erratically or checking in the pack could cause interference at a critical stage of the race.

Georginas Jet ran just six days ago and Granlahan six days ago — both are prominent types whose freshness and race sharpness will be tested, but if sound they are ideally placed to take natural positions close to Backwithyourown without having to fight for them.

High Notions carries the highest OR in the field (99) and is 26lbs clear of the minimum — watch whether the absence of a jockey listing is resolved before post time, as a strong pilot could make a material difference to how this hold-up horse is delivered.

races.name: New Forest Estate & Golf Club Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who can dictate on good ground; 232-day break is a significant flag, but trainer Rothwell has form returning horses fresh and the style-fit score of 0.93 reflects it will at least be in its preferred role — the concern is whether the layoff blunts finishing power.|

runners_data.name: Tannery Park
runners_data.note: Back after 409 days off for Barry Connell — the massive absence dominates the profile; Mark Walsh in the saddle adds confidence but the horse fades in finishes and sim-going data (8/14) is modest, making this a watch rather than a trust.|

runners_data.name: Another Glendaars
runners_data.note: J J Slevin booked for a hold-up type that has been running in good-to-firm conditions recently (27 days ago) but has posted four consecutive placed-or-worse finishes at 16f-22f with zero wins in that time — trip looks fine but finishing position has been mediocre.|

runners_data.name: Ballyglass Beauty
runners_data.note: Prominent-style mare who handles good ground (sim-going 11/15, two places) and stays well at 24f+; blinkered, which sharpens her, and Daniel — sorry, Conor Stone-Walsh keeps the ride for Cian Collins who is in fair nick at 2/15 over 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Sharetheknowledge
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied prominent type who has been off 260 days and posted four consecutive non-wins; sim-going data (11/14) is reasonable but the layoff and failure to convert good positions into wins is a persistent worry at OR 92.|

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old who has pulled up in four of his last five starts; blinkered, and won over this distance on heavy, but sim-going (5/15) is poor on good-to-firm — the P-string makes it very hard to trust at any price.|

runners_data.name: Island Mccoo
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 24f on good ground and placed over 22f on soft — the form is live, sim-going reads 9/15 with two wins and two places, and he arrives just 25 days fresh; Josh Williamson's claim helps the weight, making this one of the more attractive prominent profiles.|

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Won last time at Kilbeggan over 22f good just eight days ago — back very quickly but bouncing off a recent win and proven at the track; sim-going (8/12) with one win and three places suggests the conditions are right, and the hood/tongue-tie combo has been working.|

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: Dylan Kidd's claim reduces the load for this prominent type who has placed five times in 15 sim-going runs and showed a return to form last time (3rd, 22f, good); trainer McConnell has had a quiet 14-day spell (0/24) which tempers enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Won last time over 24f good 25 days ago and has multiple placings on similar ground — sim-going (6/15) is modest but the recent winning form is the standout; Brian Barry's 7lb claim is a genuine asset and the prominent style suits the expected race shape.|

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old hold-up type with two recent places on good ground (4th and 3rd over 22f and 20f) just 35 days ago; sim-going (3/6) is limited in sample but positive, and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable — the youth and staying profile make this a closer to monitor.|

runners_data.name: Hay Baby
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins-trained hold-up type with mixed recent form (last run 17th of 24 on good) but underlying placed form at 21f-24f on good; 61-day absence and sim-going (4/9) offering no wins give cause for caution despite the trainer's ability to freshen horses.|

runners_data.name: Coppola
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner (11/49 in 14 days — active stable) who fades in finishes and has pulled up in two of five recent starts; hold-up type who has been runner-up multiple times, especially on good, but the fade flag is a serious concern over 3m1f on quick ground.|

runners_data.name: Technology
runners_data.note: OR 84, naturally a prominent racer, but pushed into a midfield map slot by the weight of pace in this field — style-fit flags it as racing out of role, which genuinely limits its chance; recent form includes a fall and a 9th, and trainer McConnell's 14-day record (3/14) is the only positive.|

runners_data.name: Go Avel
runners_data.note: A hold-up type that fades in finishes, redistributed deeper into the map than its natural position — the combination of a fade flag and a style-fit discount (0.90) makes this one of the harder horses to back; sim-going (9/10) and a /P-949 form string confirm the profile is fragile.|

runners_data.name: Gypsy Poet
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type returning after 252 days with a form string of 96876 — zero wins, zero places in five sim-going runs (5/5), and no strong indicators of improvement; the redistribution out of natural position adds a further layer of doubt.|

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: Genuinely won over 25f on good (OR 80) and has course-going form, but has been absent just 8 days after a 7th — naturally a prominent racer displaced to midfield because the map is saturated with pace; the style-fit penalty (0.93) correctly reflects that it won't get a clean run in its preferred position.|

runners_data.name: Toor Moon
runners_data.note: Form reads 37-00U — two non-completions from the last four runs — and sim-going (10/15) is uninspiring; naturally goes up with the pace but the redistribution to midfield reflects the race won't allow it, and the form does not inspire confidence it would compete even from the right spot.|

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with a tongue-tie who is 25 days off a 7th; placed once in five sim-going runs and the form string (3F0-07) contains a fall — the youth and staying profile (placed over 26f good) are the best arguments for a late run if the race falls apart in front.|

races.paceDynamic: Down Around is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, critically, faces no serious challenger for the lead — they can roll along at a sustainable, self-selected tempo over 3m1f on good-to-firm ground. The redistribution flags on Technology, Whatyouwant, Toor Moon and others confirm this field is packed with natural prominent types who simply cannot all get their preferred berth; the most likely to actually press closest to Down Around in the first half-mile are Knocknagoran Lady, Island Mccoo and Ballyglass Beauty, though even these will be shuffled back further than they'd like. With Down Around controlling fractions unchallenged, the race is likely to be run at an honest but not punishing gallop — enough to stretch out the hold-up brigade but not enough to guarantee they get back into the race after the final bend. This shape strongly favours horses who can race in a handy position without burning energy fighting for it — true prominent types who land in the first half-dozen with something left for the climb to the last, and those with proven ability to make ground from a genuine midfield berth on good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Down Around controls, pressers strike
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around dictates an honest but measured gallop and the race is decided by those closest in the first half of the field.
scenarios.body: Down Around's uncontested lead means the race is run to suit horses that travel prominently without expending excess energy; as they begin to tire in the home straight, the nearest chasers who have conserved their running are ideally placed to pounce at the last. Horses with good-to-firm form, proven stamina at this trip, and who can secure a handy position without a fight are the chief beneficiaries — namely those with strong sim-going records and recent winning form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady pace, closers finish fast
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around's lead is truly uncontested and the early gallop is conservative, setting up a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over 3m1f compresses the field, meaning hold-up horses who survive the pace and travel well in mid-division can unleash a late run that catches the leaders cold. True closers with top-speed reserves and good-to-firm course form benefit, though the redistribution of several hold-up types to midfield means not all can deliver from their natural position, tempering confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front runner holds on wire
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around's early pace proves just strong enough to stretch and exhaust the field, leaving them alone at the last.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to apply sustained pressure, Down Around could find the fractions working perfectly in their favour — each rival using energy to close gaps while Down Around bowls along in their own rhythm. At a long trip on a flat track in good-to-firm conditions, a well-handicapped front-runner who has been off 232 days returning fresh represents a genuine danger if connections have targeted this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, crowded field splits fortunes
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 19 causes interference, traffic problems or falls that compromise several prominent horses mid-race.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over 3m1f on a track that tightens up, horses racing wide or in trouble at hurdles will lose ground they cannot recover; those who find clear runs through the middle of the field and have the stamina to outstay rivals in a messy finish benefit most. Hold-up types with the temperament to navigate traffic and the fitness to finish strongly are the accidental beneficiaries, though the redistributed hold-up horses running out of role limit confidence.

watchPoints.text: Down Around's 232-day absence is the critical unknown — if they return below peak fitness, the uncontested lead scenario collapses entirely and the whole race shape reshapes around a different pace dynamic.

Knocknagoran Lady runs just eight days after winning at this track — watch for signs of fatigue or the trainer deliberately targeting a quick back-up on the same good-to-firm ground; if fresh enough, the course advantage is real.

The 19-runner field over 3m1f on a tight track creates serious traffic-risk at hurdles; horses drawn wide or caught in the pack from the start — particularly the redistributed midfield types like Technology and Whatyouwant — may lose several lengths at early obstacles.

Coppola's fade-in-finish tag combined with Gordon Elliott's confirmed hold-up deployment over 3m1f on quick ground is a false-price trap — the horse has run second multiple times but the flag suggests this distance on this going will expose that weakness again.

Love Like This and Island Mccoo both won last time out and arrive 25 days apart respectively — two in-form prominent types who suit the expected pace shape and should be monitored from the off to see if either secures a position close enough to challenge at the second-last.
